**Package:** `dev.joid.backend.lwjgl2.snapshot` · **Module:** `backend-lwjgl2` · **Source:** [Lwjgl2SnapshotBackend.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/backend/lwjgl2/src/main/java/dev/joid/backend/lwjgl2/snapshot/Lwjgl2SnapshotBackend.java)<br/>
**Backends:** <span class="joid-badge">LWJGL 2</span>

The snapshot backend of LWJGL 2, which renders in an offscreen OpenGL context.

## Description

It renders into a pixel buffer, or into a `Display` on Linux, and ships in the dev and demo jars of the backend.

## Method details

<a id="Lwjgl2SnapshotBackend-method-create"></a>

### create

`void create(int width, int height)` 

**Throws:**

- `IllegalStateException`: LWJGL 2 cannot create the …x… OpenGL context of the snapshots (…), check that the graphics driver supports OpenGL

Installs the natives, creates the OpenGL context of that size in pixels, with 24-bit depth and 8-bit stencil, and registers the backend without audio.
Throws an `IllegalStateException` when LWJGL 2 cannot create the context.

<a id="Lwjgl2SnapshotBackend-method-destroy"></a>

### destroy

`void destroy()` 

Destroys the context and gives the registries back the bridges they had before `create`.

<a id="Lwjgl2SnapshotBackend-method-present"></a>

### present

`void present()` 

Does nothing: the capture reads the back buffer.
